editorial.headline: Industrial Metal Repair Is Open Nationally, But Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 33111 covers repair and maintenance for structural metal products, tanks, reservoirs, steam generators, and related fabricated-metal equipment.
editorial.body:
For a foreign-owned company looking at Bali, the decisive point is simple: this activity is nationally open, but the record blocks PMA registration in Bali today. KBLI 33111 sits in the repair-and-maintenance side of fabricated metal products, covering work on structural metal products, tanks, water reservoirs, metal containers, steel shipping drums, steam generators, and related steam-generator auxiliary machinery such as condensers, heaters, collectors, and steam accumulators. It also reaches specialised equipment named in the record, including nuclear reactors except isotope separators, marine engine parts, power-boiler parts, radiator work equipment, and central-heating equipment of a similar kind.

This is not a retail, advisory, or general maintenance label. Its scope is industrial and equipment-heavy: keeping fabricated-metal structures and pressure, storage, steam, and heating-related assets in working condition. The practical identity of the code is therefore repair and upkeep of metal infrastructure and machinery that already exists, rather than manufacturing new products or supplying a broad facilities-management service. The Indonesian scope is broad, but it is still bounded by the listed objects: structural metal goods, tanks and reservoirs, containers and drums, steam-generation equipment, and the specified associated machinery and parts.

On business scale, the record is unusually open. It names Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, which means the activity is available across the full scale ladder recorded here. Nationally, the PMA status is also clear: TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. In plain English, the national reading is that foreign ownership is not capped below full ownership for this activity in the record. A foreign investor analysing Indonesia at national level would therefore see a clean foreign-open classification, not a partially capped one.

Bali changes the conclusion. The Bali-side status is Blocked (risk class), and the record marks l4_bali_blocked as true. The stated reason is that OSS risk at scale Besar is Rendah/Menengah-Rendah on every scope, and that this is blocked by the Bali moratorium of May 2026. The moratorium rule in the record is island-wide and permanent: Bali province blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA. So the honest national-versus-Bali picture is not a subtle caveat. Nationally, KBLI 33111 is open to 100% foreign ownership; in Bali, a foreign-owned registration is blocked because the provincial moratorium catches this risk class.
